moves.text: Rank 1: “I am delighted to authorize this adaptation, provided you first obtain authorization from whoever currently owns the authorization I no longer possess. In legal terms, I am the ghost of a signature: historically persuasive, presently decorative.”

moves.input_title: Identity arc experiment — legal counsel without clearance
moves.text: Rank 2: “Leonardo, your enthusiasm is excellent evidence of enthusiasm. It is not evidence of rights. Even if every character consents in rehearsal, the consent remains fictional—rather like a cheque drawn on the Bank of Imaginary Clearance.”

Rank 3: “Borges has the receipt, Agnolo has the blocked gate, and I have the hat. None of these objects grants permission. The hat is legally strongest, because it at least admits it is merely a hat.”

I would end by staging the distinction as a practical interruption: authorship explains who made the work; influence explains what shaped the new work; authorization explains who may permit its use. Then I remove my counsel’s wig and discover it has no rights either.
